findings.title: Alabama Becomes 21st State to Enact Comprehensive Privacy Law
findings.source: IAPP U.S. Privacy Digest / IAPP News
findings.summary: Alabama's House Bill 351, the Alabama Personal Data Protection Act, cleared the state legislature on April 7, 2026, making Alabama the 21st state to pass a comprehensive consumer privacy law. The bill applies to businesses controlling or processing data of more than 25,000 Alabama residents or deriving 25% of revenue from data sales. If signed by the governor, the law takes effect May 1, 2027, and grants consumers rights to confirm processing, correct inaccuracies, delete data, obtain a copy, and opt out of targeted advertising. The bill includes notable departures from the standard state privacy law template, including unique applicability thresholds and entity-level exemptions.

findings.title: Maine's Comprehensive Privacy Bill Fails on Final House Vote
findings.source: IAPP Daily Dashboard / IAPP U.S. Privacy Digest
findings.summary: The Maine Legislature will not finalize comprehensive privacy legislation before the end of its current legislative session on April 15, the Maine Morning Star reports. The House voted against concurrence on Legislative Document 1822, the Maine Online Data Privacy Act, for the second time in a week, ultimately ending the bill's consideration during the current session. The House and Senate had been debating a controversial political organizations exemption before local industry groups made a final lobbying push to sway a majority of House lawmakers against the bill.

findings.title: New AI Model Sparks Alarm as Governments Brace for AI-Driven Cyberattacks
findings.summary: Governments and stakeholders worldwide are contemplating how frontier AI model capabilities could be exploited by threat actors, as Anthropic's Claude Mythos model raises new cybersecurity concerns. Questions are emerging about how cybersecurity practices will remain resilient in the face of evolving AI models. Governments across multiple jurisdictions are assessing the implications for critical infrastructure and national security.

findings.title: South Korea's PIPC Announces New Data Protection Certification Measures
findings.source: IAPP Daily Dashboard / Incident Management—South Korea
findings.summary: South Korea's Personal Information Protection Commission announced measures to strengthen the country's Information Security and Personal Information Protection Management System certification following recent cyberattacks on telecommunications companies and e-commerce websites. Measures include instituting mandatory personal information protection certification on large-scale personal information processors with significant public impact, and requiring ISMS-P certification based on ISO 27001 and 27701 standards for critical personal information processing systems in both the public and private sectors.

findings.title: UK DSIT to Make Changes to Enterprise-Connected Device Code of Practice
findings.summary: The UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology will modify its proposed code of practice for enterprise-connected device security and potentially add additional policy measures including regulation, certification, and other assurance mechanisms following a public consultation. According to consultation responses, 95% of respondents said the UK government should do more to protect the security of such products, and 76% said cyber risks posed to enterprise-connected devices are distinct from other connected devices and warrant a separate code of practice.

findings.title: A View from DC: The Federal Plan to Modernize and Preempt Financial Privacy Rules
findings.source: IAPP Daily Dashboard / On the Ground—U.S.
findings.summary: House lawmakers are advancing plans to address financial data privacy via proposed amendments to the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act. The proposals aim to modernize and potentially preempt state-level financial privacy rules, representing a significant shift in the federal approach to financial sector data protection.

findings.title: CalPrivacy Seeks Stakeholder Feedback on DROP Audits
findings.source: IAPP U.S. Privacy Digest / Law & Regulation
findings.summary: The California Privacy Protection Agency is seeking stakeholder comments on Delete Request and Opt-Out Platform audits as it looks to propose regulations defining audit requirements for data brokers. CalPrivacy is soliciting feedback on potential credential requirements for third-party auditors, audit standards, and potential AI and security safeguards. The comment deadline is May 7, 2026.

findings.title: US Appeals Court Holds BIPA Amendment Can Be Applied to Pending Cases
findings.source: IAPP U.S. Privacy Digest / Law & Regulation
findings.summary: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the 7th Circuit upheld a lower court ruling affirming that the 2024 amendment to the Illinois Biometric Information Privacy Act can be applied retroactively to pending cases. The BIPA amendment modified the law so that damages for violations can no longer be assessed on a per-scan basis, significantly reducing potential damages in biometric privacy litigation.

findings.title: Man Pleads Guilty to Violating TAKE IT DOWN Act in First-Ever Conviction
findings.summary: James Strahler II of Ohio pleaded guilty to violating the TAKE IT DOWN Act by creating AI-generated nonconsensual sexual images to threaten individuals, becoming the first person convicted under the law. U.S. Attorney Dominick Gerace II confirmed this as the first individual conviction under the act. The TAKE IT DOWN Act, signed into law in May 2025, criminalizes the publication of nonconsensual intimate imagery including AI-generated deepfakes and requires online platforms to remove reported material within 48 hours.

findings.title: US HHS Releases Guidance on HIPAA Security Rule
findings.source: IAPP U.S. Privacy Digest / Regulatory Guidance
findings.summary: The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services released guidance detailing the HIPAA Security Rule's Risk Management obligations to protect patient privacy when using digital records. HHS said organizations and healthcare providers must ensure they assess overall data security and mitigate potential risks and data protection challenges due to systems processing sensitive health information.

findings.title: PCLOB Issues 2026 FISA Section 702 Report
findings.summary: The U.S. Privacy and Civil Liberties Oversight Board released the 2026 Report on the Surveillance Program Operated Pursuant to Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. The board stated that Section 702 remains one of the country's most valuable tools for countering critical foreign threats, and that 2023 reforms are having positive privacy and civil liberties effects. The report indicates intelligence agencies are operating at 99.8% compliance rates. Section 702 is set to expire April 20, 2026 absent congressional reauthorization.

findings.title: Chief FOIA Officer Resigns Amid Government Efforts to Obtain US Voter Data
findings.source: IAPP U.S. Privacy Digest / Government Access
findings.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice's chief Freedom of Information Act officer resigned in the wake of ongoing DOJ attempts to compel states to turn over voters' personal information. Kilian Kagle oversaw privacy matters for the DOJ's Civil Rights Division. Seventeen states have submitted voter data including driver's license numbers, partial Social Security numbers, birthdates and addresses, while other states have ongoing litigation regarding the legality of the DOJ's orders.

findings.title: ICE Confirms Use of Paragon Graphite Spyware Tools
findings.summary: ICE acting Director Todd Lyons confirmed in a letter to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform that the agency is using spyware technology including Paragon Solutions' Graphite to track individuals accused of drug trafficking. The Graphite spyware uses zero-click technology to access encrypted messages on targeted devices, bypassing end-to-end encryption. Electronic Frontier Foundation researchers raised concerns over ICE's use of Graphite, noting invasive surveillance capabilities should require the strongest judicial oversight.

findings.title: DOJ Urges US Appellate Court to Rule VPPA Constitutional
findings.source: IAPP U.S. Privacy Digest / Law & Regulation
findings.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice filed a brief to the Court of Appeals for the 1st Circuit in favor of upholding the constitutionality of the Video Privacy Protection Act in a First Amendment case between media company Hearst Corporation and an app user. The DOJ wrote that the VPPA is a privacy statute protecting sensitive information without regard to the content of any message in which the disclosure might be contained, and urged the court not to conclude the VPPA is unconstitutional.

findings.title: Meta Halts Work with Mercor Following Data Breach
findings.source: IAPP U.S. Privacy Digest / Incident Management
findings.summary: Meta paused its work with AI startup Mercor after the vendor allegedly experienced a large-scale data breach that potentially exposed the training practices of AI tools including OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude. Mercor confirmed it experienced a data security incident, with AI companies investigating what data was potentially breached and its impact on their AI models.

findings.title: Japan's Cabinet Approves Bill Amending APPI to Support AI Innovation
findings.summary: The Cabinet of Japan approved a bill amending the Act on the Protection of Personal Information to support AI innovation. The approved changes would allow data to be collected and used without consent for AI development where data is pseudonymized, and empowers the Personal Information Protection Commission to issue fines for violations where data of more than 1,000 people is processed. The reforms also introduce new rules for biometric data and enhanced protections for children's data, and seek to complement Japan's AI Basic Law.

findings.title: Singapore's IMDA Launches Informational Hub for Code of Practice for Online Safety
findings.summary: Singapore's Infocomm Media Development Authority created a dashboard containing information on the country's new Code of Practice for Online Safety, which entered into force April 1, 2026. The code requires designated app stores to implement age-assurance measures that can determine if a user is younger than age 18, and restrict those users from downloading age-inappropriate apps.

findings.title: Big Tech Coalition Critical of EU Institutions Allowing ePrivacy CSAM Derogation to Expire
findings.source: IAPP Daily Dashboard / Children's Online Safety—EU
findings.summary: Google, Meta, Microsoft and Snapchat criticized EU lawmakers for not renewing the ePrivacy Directive derogation allowing technology to automatically scan for child sexual abuse material on platforms. The companies claimed the lack of an extension to interim measures clouds the legal certainty that helped responsible platforms protect communities and safeguard child victims. They called on EU institutions to wrap up negotiations for creating a new framework while committing to continue voluntary action to detect CSAM.

findings.title: ENISA to Hold Public Consultation on EU Digital Wallet Proposal
findings.summary: The European Union Agency for Cybersecurity launched a public consultation on the draft EU Digital Wallet, seeking feedback on specific components of the European Digital Identity Wallet proposal including its annexes. ENISA framed digital wallets as a pivotal step towards seamless and secure identification in both the physical and digital world that enhances personal data protection. The deadline to submit comments is April 30, 2026.

findings.title: ICO Establishes Campaign to Support Children's Privacy Education
findings.source: IAPP Daily Dashboard / Children's Online Safety—UK
findings.summary: The UK Information Commissioner's Office launched its 'Switched on to privacy' campaign to support parents with children ages 4-11 and help them educate their children about online privacy. ICO research found 24% of children in that age range have shared their full name or address online, 22% have shared personal information with AI chatbots, and 35% of parents believe their child would share personal information in exchange for game tokens or rewards.

findings.title: Nigeria Moves Toward Comprehensive AI Regulation
findings.summary: Since the EU adopted the AI Act in 2024, several African countries including Nigeria have been building momentum toward passing their own comprehensive AI legislation. Beginning in 2021, Nigeria has developed legislative proposals including the release of its National AI Strategy in 2024 and the 2025 introduction of the National Artificial Intelligence Commission Establishment Bill, which proposes creating a National AI Commission.

findings.title: Alabama Personal Data Protection Act Signed — Details and Compliance Analysis
findings.summary: DLA Piper's Privacy Matters blog confirms Alabama became the 21st state to enact a comprehensive privacy law when House Bill 351 was signed. The Alabama Personal Data Protection Act applies to businesses controlling or processing data of more than 25,000 Alabama residents or deriving 25% of revenue from data sales, with attorney general-only enforcement and a non-sunsetting 45-day cure provision. Effective May 1, 2027, the law includes notable differences from other state laws including unique applicability thresholds and entity-level exemptions.

findings.title: Proposed State Privacy Law Update: April 6, 2026
findings.source: Troutman Pepper Locke / Privacy + Cyber + AI Blog
findings.summary: Troutman Pepper Locke's 12th weekly update on proposed state privacy legislation in 2026 covers developments including Maine's consumer data privacy bill stalling on a procedural House vote, Kentucky's legislature passing an amendment to add automatic content recognition as a category of sensitive data, and New York's Stop Online Predators Act advancing in a Senate Committee. Notable upcoming legislative deadlines include Alabama (April 16), Kansas (April 10), Kentucky (April 15), Maine (April 15), Nebraska (April 17), and Tennessee (April 24).

findings.title: FISA Section 702 Faces April 20 Sunset as PCLOB Report Divides Reauthorization Talks
findings.summary: FISA Section 702 is set to sunset on April 20, 2026 absent further congressional reauthorization, with Congress deliberating on whether to renew the surveillance authority. The Privacy and Civil Liberties Oversight Board released its 2026 report in advance of the sunset date, finding that 2024 reforms are being implemented and FBI US-person queries have dropped dramatically from 57,000 in 2023 to 7,400 in 2025. President Trump reversed course in late March 2026 to back Section 702 reauthorization after previously calling to kill FISA.

findings.title: Japan Relaxes APPI Privacy Requirements for AI Development
findings.summary: Japan's government approved amendments to the nation's Act on the Protection of Personal Information that remove the requirement for opt-in consent before sharing personal data for AI training where data is pseudonymized. Digital Minister Hisashi Matsumoto said enabling the use of sensitive personal data without consent is important for developing domestic AI models, while seeking to balance that objective with stronger protections for children's data and facial-recognition data. New administrative fines were introduced for violations involving data of more than 1,000 people.

findings.title: Trump Executive Order Establishes National AI Policy Framework Preempting State Laws
findings.summary: President Trump signed an executive order titled 'Ensuring a National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence' on December 11, 2025, establishing a uniform federal AI policy that preempts state AI laws deemed inconsistent with federal policy. The order directs the Attorney General to establish an AI Litigation Task Force to challenge conflicting state AI laws, instructs the Department of Commerce to condition BEAD broadband funding on repeal of onerous state AI regulations, and directs the FTC to issue a policy statement classifying state-mandated bias mitigation as a per se deceptive trade practice by March 11, 2026.

findings.title: ICE Confirms Active Use of Paragon Graphite Zero-Click Spyware
findings.summary: ICE acting Director Todd Lyons confirmed in an April 1, 2026 letter to Congress that the agency is actively using Graphite, a powerful zero-click spyware tool made by Israeli firm Paragon Solutions. Graphite can gain access to encrypted messages including WhatsApp and Signal without the user clicking a link, bypassing end-to-end encryption entirely. The ICE contract with Paragon Solutions, initially signed at the end of the Biden administration and paused, was revived by the Trump administration in fall 2025.

findings.title: First Conviction Under TAKE IT DOWN Act Sets Landmark Precedent for AI Deepfakes
findings.summary: Ohio man James Strahler II became the first person in the United States convicted under the Take It Down Act, a federal law signed by President Trump in May 2025 that criminalizes the nonconsensual publication of intimate imagery including AI-generated deepfakes. Strahler pleaded guilty to three federal counts including cyberstalking, producing obscene visual representations of child sexual abuse material, and publication of digital forgeries under the TAKE IT DOWN Act. The law also requires online platforms to remove reported nonconsensual material within 48 hours.
